creator: Jacob Rees-Mogg
title: The ruin of Britain. Starmer out, Miliband in.
full_text:
For some time, it's been a question of
when, not if, it is over for Secure
Star. His premiership is in its dying
days, its last throws, its final
breaths. It may be appropriate that the
assisted dying bill is still going
through parliament because his
premiership is dying. And this isn't
particularly good for the country
because the country drifts when it needs
leadership. The final problem, the end
is of course Peter Mandlesson and that
secure Starmer knew that Peter
Mandlesson had maintained a relationship
with Jeffrey Epstein after Epstein had
been found guilty of molesting a child.
A child. It's easy to forget in the
political excitement what a revolting
individual Epstein was and how terrible
and criminal his behavior was. He was a
pedophile and that is one of the
nastiest, most unpleasant, most shocking
of crimes. And Peter Mandlesson remained
in contact with him after he had been
found guilty of these crimes. There was
no longer any claim that he was somebody
just with a dodgy reputation. He was
somebody who'd been found guilty in a
court of law and sentenced to a period
of imprisonment. That was the sleas that
Mandlesson was involved with, remained
involved with, continued to be involved
with, and K star knew it. There is
something
disobliging about the efforts of people
to run away from Peter Mandlesson who
depended upon him beforehand who were
desperate for his patronage wanted his
friendship enjoyed his company but now
it's as if they never knew him they
never liked him they never wanted to be
in his presence all these labor people
who were deeply entwined with Peter
Mandlesson are now pretending they
hardly knew his name but That is false.
It is untrue. It is a further attempt to
mislead the public as they run away from
one of the worst scandals in modern
British political history. What do you
think of in comparison? Well, you think
of Profumo and you think of the Maronei
scandal, a financial scandal surrounding
Lloyd George, which was covered up
pretty effectively by a whitewash
parliamentary inquiry. So it's a deep
scandal and Stalmer knew too much too
early for it to be possible to exculpate
him. So that leads to the question of
who next. And that's a very interesting
question. And here I can speak purely as
an observer because I have no say in who
Labour will choose. Labor figures won't
listen to me. I'm watching in exactly
the same way as you, my viewers, are
watching it as an interested and I hope
informed observer, seeing the pieces of
the jigsaw puzzle fit together. So,
what's piece number one? Piece number
one is that Andrew Burnham is out. It's
too late for him to get selected for the
bi-election in Manchester and Labour's
going to be hammered in that
bi-election. I'm not allowed to talk
about this on GB news because of crazy
regulations and laws surrounding what
you can say on public broadcast uh on
bi-elections, but I can I can speak
freely on YouTube. Labor will be
hammered. It's between the Greens and
Reform. The Conservative Party has a
respectable candidate who I obviously
wish well, but I'd be astonished if the
Conservatives manage to make a
breakthrough in this. And Labour may get
less than 10% of the vote. It may be a
real calamity for Labor in a seat that
it held with over 50% in 2024 and over
twothirds of the vote on a simulation on
those boundaries for 2019. It's a
catastrophe for Labor.
But Andy Burnham will not be part of it.
He will not be getting into parliament.
He won't be eligible to stand for
leadership. So Stal has done one thing.
He has knobbled the front runner. So who
does that leave? Well, today Angela
Raina is the first to involve herself in
moves against Starmmer trying to make
life more difficult for him on the
humble address. The humble address is a
fascinating piece of parliamentary
procedure. It was popular in the 19th
century and then fell out of use. It
ceases to be mentioned in Urskin May I
think beyond the 12th edition. But a
humble address requires the government
to produce papers. It can only
effectively be used when a government is
in a minority, has a very slim majority,
or as in this case, a big majority has
evaporated. Shows the weakness of Labor
in Parliament that they had to give in
to a humble address. But Angela Raina's
been stirring things up for Star. But
surely she can't become leader of the
party because Angela Raina is mired in
her own scandal which has not gone away.
How could Labour after Peter Mandlesson
has been shown to have been leaking
government secrets from a man who gave
him money? A financial scandal of the
worst order. Then turn as leader to
somebody who has admittedly a lesser but
nonetheless a financial scandal of her
own. I just don't think voters are going
to accept a new prime minister who
didn't pay her taxes at this point when
Labour has been exposed for being a
party of financial corruption. What
Manderson's done isn't sleas, it's
corruption as I discussed with David
Starky in the Starky and Mog that will
be released today.
So I think that rules her out. I think
the Labour Party will realize that that
is impossible and I accept that what she
did is not criminal. I accept that what
she did could have been a mistake. But
nonetheless, she failed to pay the due
tax. And that seems to me to rule her
out
in current circumstances. It just seems
wrong to take somebody with a financial
scandal after Mandlesson's experience.
So who next? Well, where's Streing?
Wes Streeting is capable man,
intelligent individual. Actually, let's
say nice things about Angela Raina, too.
Um, charismatic individual,
clear views of what she wants to do, a
big personality in politics. I'm not
attacking these people as individuals,
as people, but simply as whether or not
they can be fit for office. And where
streeting was a great friend of Peter
Mandlesson's he was writhing today to
say that he didn't like Peter Mandles
anymore that Peter Mandlesson wasn't a
friend of his to disassociate himself
from any connection to Peter Mandlesson
who was his sort of mentor previously
whom he was very close to he was very
pleased to have speak in his
constituency when he was running for
parliament and you don't tend to have
people come and speak in your
constituency
who you don't like and admire. Partly
they're the only ones who come your
friends and partly those are the only
ones that you invite. So
Mandlesson taints Wes Streetine to a
point where I think electing him becomes
impossible. that Labour may not realize
or certainly new labor ites such as
remain may not realize quite how this
has tarnished their whole brand the
whole Blairite project and this sticks
to West Streeting whether fairly or
unfairly like glue and I don't see how
he can be leader he's also on the right
of the party and I'd be very surprised
if the Labour party wanted to move
rightwards from its current position.
Then you've got Shabbana Mimmude. Well,
Shabbana Shabbana Mammud, the home
secretary, was the first socialist in a
long time to say something sensible
about immigration. If you read today's
papers, 50 Labor MPs have said they
impose her immigration reforms. And they
won't be possible anyway
without
leaving the European Convention on Human
Rights and repealing the Human Rights
Act, or at least amending it. And
there's no way Labour's going to do
that. So I think Shabbana Mammud can't
get it because again like West treating
she's too rightwing. She's not tainted
by Star, but she is too rightwing for
the mood of the Labor Party. She's
actually too good for Labor in terms of
migration. And I doubt she'll thank me
for saying she's too good. I think she's
a capable minister, has been saying some
sensible things, but actually she
wouldn't be able to do them unless she
joined reform, which I imagine she
doesn't wish to do. I think she's not
the high-profile defector from the
Labour Party that has been trailed by
reform. So, who does that leave? Well,
it leaves the one and only Ed Milliband,
the once and future leader of the Labor
Party. Why? Well, he's popular with
Labourist. He's popular with Labour
members. He will become popular with
Labor MPs because an awful lot of MPs
back the person they think will win. And
that leads to momentum. was hugely
helpful to Boris's campaign that his
popularity in the party at large meant
that lots of MPs wanted to support him
because they felt if they got in early
then they might get some office from him
they might got some role in a Boris
administration that will be happening
with Milliban people will look at the
arithmetic and they will say look he
wins with the public we can't have Raina
because of sleas we can't have streeting
because of star we can't have Shabbana
because actually she's too sensible
Well, so it and he gets all the votes
from Labour members. That's the first
point. But, and this is hugely to his
credit, he is one of the Labour leaders
over the last 30 years, slightly more,
who would have absolutely nothing to do
with Peter Mandlesson.
So, when um Ed Milliband became leader
of the Labour Party, Mandlesson played
no role in it. Whereas he did for Neil
Kinnock, he didn't for John Smith. He
was central to new labor for Blair and
for Brown. And then Milliband wouldn't
have him. And then it has to be said
Jeremy Corbyn wouldn't have him, but
he's no longer a member of the Labour
Party and Starmmer brought him back in
spite of all the scandals.
I'm not going to advise you to go down
to the bookmakers. Betting on politics
went rather wrong when it happened
during the general election. say that's
not what I'm going to suggest, but I
would say I think Ed Milliband is the
most likely next leader of the Labour
Party. I think it could happen quite
soon.
I think his views on green policy are
disastrous
and would be very bad for the country.
But I will say this and it'll drive you
all mad because you don't like me saying
nice things about socialists, but at
least we'd have an honest man as prime
minister. He may not be my ideological
soulmate. Indeed, he's almost the exact
opposite. But I wouldn't doubt his
honesty or his integrity. And that might
be rather better than the sleas fest
that we've had for the last 18 months.
As always, thank you very much for
watching.

notes.note: Erskine May still covers humble addresses. The current 25th edition (2019) includes Section 9.10 'Addresses to the Crown' and Section 7.31 on calling for papers by humble address stating motions are made as 'That an humble Address be presented to Her Majesty'.

sources.quote: Usually, the motion for an Address is made in the form ‘That an humble Address be presented to Her Majesty to …’ and the necessary prefatory words[3](#footnote-item-3) are inserted when the actual copy of the Address is prepared.
sources.explanation: Shows the exact motion wording claimed in the note.

sources.quote: Returns may be called for by an Order or an humble Address, and it is not always clear which is appropriate.
sources.explanation: Shows para 7.31 covers calling for papers by humble Address.

sources.quote: A return from the Privy Council or from departments headed by a Secretary of State is usually called for by means of a motion on the Order Paper for an humble Address.
sources.explanation: Shows humble Address is the usual means for calling for papers from Privy Council / Secretary of State departments.
